contentBlocks.text: Means Test Failed — What It Means

The 'Means Test Failed' status means that SASSA's financial assessment determined your income or assets exceed the legal maximum for the grant you applied for. The means test is a financial eligibility check that ensures grants go to South Africans who genuinely need financial support.
This status affects applicants whose declared income or assets exceeded SASSA's means test threshold.

contentBlocks.title: Need a full explanation of the means test?
contentBlocks.text: Our comprehensive guide explains income thresholds, asset limits, the sliding scale, and how SASSA calculates your eligibility in detail.

contentBlocks.explanation: SASSA evaluates your income and assets against published legal thresholds. If either your income or assets exceed the limit for your specific grant, your application is declined for means test failure.
whyItHappens: Your annual income exceeds the threshold for single applicants (R96,240 for most grants)
Your combined household income exceeds the married threshold (R192,480)
Your assets (property, investments, savings, vehicles) exceed the asset limit (R1,372,800 single, R2,745,600 married)
For SRD: your bank account received deposits exceeding R624 in a single month
You declared income or assets on your application that exceed the limits
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: The decline applies to the current application or monthly cycle. You can reapply or appeal if your financial situation has changed or if SASSA's assessment was incorrect.
whatYouShouldDo: Review the means test thresholds for your specific grant on the Grant Library page
Check if SASSA may have incorrectly calculated your income or assets
If your financial situation has changed: submit updated bank statements and financial records
If SASSA made an error: file an appeal with evidence showing your actual income/assets
If your income legitimately exceeds thresholds: you may not qualify for this grant at this time

faqs.question: What counts as income for the means test?
faqs.answer: Salary/wages, pension payments, rental income, farm income, regular gifts or remittances, UIF payments, NSFAS allowances, and interest from investments.

faqs.question: What counts as assets?
faqs.answer: Property (excluding the home you live in), investments, savings accounts, shares, vehicles, and any other valuable assets you own.

faqs.question: Can I appeal a means test failure?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you believe SASSA miscalculated your income or assets, file an appeal with supporting financial documents within 90 days.

faqs.question: I was approved before but now my status says means test failed. Why?
faqs.answer: Every month is reassessed. If your financial situation changed (e.g., you received a deposit or started earning), you may fail the means test in subsequent months.
